title: A lane cannot close a PR; the runner is the only closer, after the archive copy
why: Lane ci-mac-once-per-batch closed #3088 before the coordinator's line reached it (coordinator 22:44 CST Nov 13, relayed, unchecked). Branch drop-nightly-schedule is intact on origin at 4344c60c07; nothing lost.
note: Triage 22:44 CST Nov 13: guard idea, not built. The rule says runner 10 is the only closer and archive-first applies; no check stops a lane from closing a PR. Mistake it stops: a lane closing a PR on its own. Harm if repeated: a stacked PR closed with its base branch not archived. Check candidate: the GitHub close act (MCP update_pull_request with state closed) refuses in a lane session and names the runner. Triage read the rule from the coordinator's text, not the decision; needs a past-ruling and guard-record read, and a look at how often lanes close PRs on the record, before any build. Another instance 23:53 CST Nov 13 (coordinator 23:53, relayed; lane message 23:52, not re-read): lane cloud-snapshot-age-check closed #3263 itself, because the merge tool's remedy for a pushed commit with a bad Red-run trailer was "a replacement PR" (replacement is draft #3370, head ad3f64ec351c). The remedy text could say "ask the batch runner to close the old PR": runner 10 is the only closer.
